Forward deployed engineering is one of the
hardest roles to assess
Every company defines the role differently. Some want a production engineer on site with the customer, others a solution architect who scopes the work and hands it off. A generic coding test covers only half of either job.
What sets a strong FDE apart happens before and after the coding: finding the customer’s real problem, and handing over cleanly to the next engineer or coding agent.
FDEs ship with coding agents, so a take-home without AI tests a job that no longer exists. With AI allowed, the finished code shows little about how the candidate directed the agent.
One assessment that follows the job: plan, build, communicate
Plan: scope an unclear customer request
The candidate reads a customer’s request, the system documentation and what the system actually does. They decide what to build, what to ask first and which decisions belong to the customer. Their written plan is scored against defined criteria.
Build in Python with Claude Code or Codex
A hands-on Python task in a full VS Code IDE, such as a retrieval pipeline that answers questions from a store of documents. Candidates use the real Claude Code or Codex when you allow it, with AI usage included and no API keys to set up. Hidden tests score the result.
Communicate: explain the trade-offs to the customer
The candidate writes the recommendation for a stakeholder who does not code: what changed, what it costs in scope, speed and quality, and what the customer has to decide. Every candidate is scored by the same rules.
See how each candidate works with coding agents
Each part of the assessment gets its own score, so a strong coder who skipped the scoping stands out. Read what the candidate asked the agent and what they changed before accepting its answer.

The five skills every FDE role shares
Codility’s assessment science team reviewed forward deployed engineer job descriptions at enterprise companies. Five skills appear in every one: scoping a customer problem when the request is unclear, production software engineering in Python, building with AI models and agents, owning delivery end to end, and communicating with technical and business stakeholders.
Skills such as checking how an AI system performs once it is live, enterprise integration or knowledge of a specific platform matter far more at some companies than at others. The assessment science team adds them when your role needs them.

FDEs use coding agents every day on the job, so an assessment without AI tests a job that no longer exists. Codility includes Claude Code and Codex in the assessment and shows how each candidate used them.
